title: The Complicated Politics of Trump’s Medical Cannabis Policies

content_html_sanitized:
It’s clear that President Trump wants to loosen up the restrictions on medical cannabis.

 

First, he has said that it would be popular, which doesn’t require a political genius to see, when almost 90% of the American people are in favor of it.

 

Plus he has been lobbied by some famous friends.

See Politicians Who Question Whether Athletes Need Recreational Cannabis Should Have To Go Few Rounds With Mike Tyson

 

So, it should be easy, especially after the 2020 election.

See

The Sad Case For Biden Over Trump For Medical Marijuana Users

And

Did Marijuana Prohibition Cost Trump the Election Once and the Democrats Twice?

 

The problem gets more complicated at the appointed staff level. Unfortunately the ideologues that are usually appointed to fill these positions, like the head of the DEA, and the “experts” for their staff are mostly true believer Reefer Madness fans.

 

For example, the relevant staff in almost all of the Washington pro-business think tanks are hard core Prohibitionist ideologues.

See

How The Heritage Foundation Used Newsweek to Recycle Lies About My “Medical Marijuana Scam”

And

Heritage and Harvard and the War on Truth and Freedom

 

Right now these ideologues are tied in knots desperately trying to stop cannabis from being moved from Schedule 1 (no medical use) to Schedule 3, which they say would send the wrong message to children, etc, etc, etc.

See

Dr. Carson, This Isn’t Brain Surgery. Please Let Us Use Our Brains for Ourselves

 

Almost the only exception has been the libertarian Cato Institute. Its executive vice president, the late David Boaz served on the NORML board of directors when I was National Director, and no one from Cato would fit in at the DEA.

 

Consequently, Trump is torn between the realist cynics  and the fundamentalist cynics. And if you’re not a cynic at this point, you are not paying attention.

See

President Trump Promotes CBD and Medical Cannabis on Truth Social! And That Is Just the Beginning!

 

Finally, it may just be a problem with there being too many problems. Everyone in the White House may really need medical cannabis after this week.

See

'Trump effect' raises hopes for cannabis rally as investors bet on federal reforms, softer marijuana stance
